calculator.titleTail: It multiplies the size of your mistake.
calculator.intro: Change any field and the rest follow. Type into profit and loss instead, and the close price is solved backwards from it.
calculator.pnlHint: Type a target here and the close price is solved for it.

tips.amount: Your own money put into the trade: the margin, in USDT. Leverage multiplies it into the position size. Type it here or in units of the asset — the other side follows at the open price.
tips.openPrice: The price the position is entered at.
tips.closePrice: The price you plan to exit at. Change it to see the profit or loss, or type a target into profit / loss and this is solved for you.
tips.leverage: How many times the position is larger than your margin. 10× turns 100 into a 1000 position: gains and losses both move ten times faster.
tips.pnl: Profit or loss when closing at the close price, before fees and funding. Long profits when the price rises, short when it falls.
tips.amountUnits: The same margin counted in units of the asset: USDT ÷ open price. Leverage does not change it. Type either side and the other follows.

risk.heading: What this position actually is
risk.roiNote: Against the money you put up
risk.disclaimer: Simplified: maintenance margin, fees and funding all bring liquidation closer than shown. Treat these as a ceiling, not a promise.

tips.positionSize: Amount × leverage: how much of the asset you actually control. Fees and funding are charged on this, not on your amount.
tips.roi: Profit or loss as a percentage of the margin you put up. With leverage this moves far faster than the price itself.
tips.liquidationMove: How far the price can go against you before the whole margin is gone: roughly 100% ÷ leverage.
tips.liquidationPrice: The price at which the exchange would close the position and keep your margin. Below entry for a long, above it for a short.

info.intro: None of this is advice. It is arithmetic that stays true whatever the market does.
info.liquidationBody: At 25× a 4% move against you wipes the whole margin. At 100× it takes 1%. The higher the leverage, the tighter the stop the exchange sets on your behalf — and it does not ask first.
info.feesBody: Commission and funding are charged on the notional, not on your money. At 25× you pay twenty-five times what the amount suggests, whether the trade wins or loses.
info.asymmetryBody: Down 50% needs up 100% to get back to even. Down 80% needs 400%. Leverage moves you along that curve much faster than it moves you back.

footer.tagline: Profit and loss, without the spreadsheet
footer.disclaimer: A calculator, not financial advice. Figures are simplified and ignore fees, funding and maintenance margin.

spot.titleTail: See where it lands before you click.
spot.intro: Enter what you hold and the price you paid on average. Add a planned buy to see the new average, then set a sale price to see what the whole position would make.
spot.salePriceHint: The price you want to sell the whole position at.
spot.saleValueNote: Every unit at the sale price
spot.disclaimer: Simplified: trading fees on the buy and the sale are not included, so the real break-even sits slightly above the average.

tips.quantity: How many units of the asset you hold right now, e.g. 0.5 BTC. Type it here or as the USDT invested — the other follows at the average price.
tips.averagePrice: What you paid per unit on average across all your previous buys. Exchanges usually call it average cost or entry price.
tips.buyQuantity: How many more units you plan to buy. Type it here or as the USDT to spend — the other follows at the buy price. Leave it at 0 to see just your current position.
tips.buyPrice: Price per unit for the planned buy. Buying below your average pulls it down; buying above pushes it up.
tips.salePrice: The price you want to exit at. The whole position is assumed sold here: the units you hold and the ones you plan to buy.
tips.newAverage: Total invested divided by total units. This is your break-even: selling above it is profit, below it is loss.
tips.totalQuantity: Units you hold now plus the units from the planned buy.
tips.totalCost: What all the units cost you: units held × average price, plus units bought × buy price.
tips.saleValue: Total units × sale price: what you would receive, before fees.
tips.pnl: Sale value minus total invested. The percentage is measured against total invested.
tips.pnlWithoutBuy: The same sale price applied to your current position only, so you can see whether the planned buy helps or hurts.
tips.invested: What your current units cost in total: units × average price. Type it here or as units — the other follows.
tips.buyCost: How much USDT the planned buy takes: units × buy price. Type it here or as units — the other follows.
